Adds an IPv4 address or Class C CIDR range by attempting to add aliases to the main network interface. It rebuilds /etc/ipaddrpool, stores addresses in /etc/ips and uses ipaliases to activate them at startup. The documented CIDR range mask is 24 through 30. These changes can affect server networking.

Supply excludes as a raw comma-delimited address string or a nonempty sequential string list. Omission excludes no addresses; the multiple-address example includes an inconsistent excludes= prefix, while the parameter description specifies the address list itself. The client forwards the supplied value once without adding a prefix or validating network syntax.
This void method leaves the pinned metadata.output.messages string list in responseMeta()->whm['output']['messages']; inspect that metadata for per-address output after envelope success.

Client list convenience: accept a nonempty sequential list of strict strings and join once with a comma into the original field. Preserve order, duplicates, empty items and all other bytes; reject embedded commas and malformed or empty lists after metadata reset before I/O. Raw scalars remain unparsed and encoded once. Collection arguments have trace protection without changing transport. Offline coverage only; historical scalar captures do not establish PHP-list execution.
